VZ.rationale: Verizon presents a mildly-to-moderately attractive fundamental case. The franchise is durable — narrow-moat U.S. wireless triopoly with ~38% market share, 94M+ postpaid phone subscribers, and $18.7B FCF in 2024. Q1 2026 showed improving execution: first positive Q1 postpaid phone net additions since 2013, +2.9% YoY revenue growth, +4.3% EPS growth, and raised full-year guidance. The Frontier acquisition doubled fiber passings to 25M homes, and FWA has scaled to 4.8M+ subscribers, providing modest growth levers in a mature market. Valuation is the primary attraction: P/E of 11.4x sits at the floor of its 365-day range (11.0–21.2x) versus a historical median of ~17–18x, and the 8.8% earnings yield offers a 435bps spread over the 10Y Treasury. However, the extreme P/E compression likely reflects justified market skepticism: the net margin jump from 7.6% to 12.8% appears as a single-date ratio observation with no TTM composition available to verify durability, and organic growth is flat absent Frontier's contribution. The ~$120B debt load and 3.0x liabilities/equity constrain flexibility. Rising rates (+40bps on 10Y over 90 days) are a mechanical headwind for yield-oriented equities. The score is capped at +0.25 rather than higher because: (1) the margin sustainability question is unresolved and the re-rating math cannot be validated without TTM EPS, (2) organic growth remains thin, and (3) leverage limits financial flexibility. The positive postpaid trends and cheap valuation provide a modest fundamental floor.
key_factors: P/E diluted of 11.4x on 2026-05-28 is at the floor of its 365-day range (11.0–21.2x), far below the ~17–18x median seen in late 2025/early 2026
Earnings yield of 8.8% provides a 435bps spread over the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.45%
Q1 2026 revenue $34.44B (+2.9% YoY), EPS diluted $1.20 (+4.3% YoY), operating income $8.24B (+3.3% YoY)
First positive Q1 postpaid phone net additions since 2013; full-year guidance raised to top half of 750K–1M range
Net margin ratio jumped from 7.6% to 12.8% and ROE from 10.5% to 17.0% as single-date observations on 2026-05-28 — durability unverifiable without TTM composition
Frontier acquisition ($20B, completed 2025) doubled fiber passings to ~25M homes; FWA scaled to 4.8M+ subscribers
~$120B total debt with 3.0x liabilities/equity; $4B notes offering in May 2026; management targets 2.0x net debt/EBITDA
10Y yield rose from 4.05% to 4.45% (+40bps in 90 days), a mechanical headwind for dividend/yield plays
Morningstar narrow moat based on U.S. wireless triopoly efficient-scale dynamics (VZ ~38%, T-Mobile ~34%, AT&T ~28%)
Organic growth closer to flat without Frontier contribution; competitive pressure from T-Mobile and cable MVNOs persists

sources_cited.excerpt: Verizon highlighted positive postpaid phone net additions in the first quarter of 2026, including its first positive 1Q postpaid phone net additions since 2013 and guidance raised to the top half of a 750,000–1 million range for the year.

Total operating revenues reached $34.44 billion, up from $33.49 billion a year earlier…diluted earnings per share increased to $1.20 from $1.15…the underlying organic growth rate would have been closer to flat without the Frontier acquisition.

Free Cash Flow reached 18.7 billion dollars in 2024 and management expects a similar trajectory in 2025…Adjusted EBITDA margins remain healthy at about 35 percent…cost programs that have cut over 3 billion dollars in annual operating expenses.
In 2025, Verizon accelerated a strategic shift by acquiring Frontier Communications for $20,000,000,000…Frontier deal raises fiber passing to 25 million homes.

We assign Verizon a narrow moat based on the wireless industry's efficient scale characteristics. With three sizable players, we don't believe the major carriers will have an incentive to aggressively poach each other's customers over the long term.
The FCC approved a roughly 1 billion USD spectrum purchase from U.S. Cellular…Verizon generated higher revenue year over year and posted a net margin of 12.46% with return on equity of 19.25%.
